Public Contracts Directive defines thresholds triggering full directive application
Utilities Directive defines higher thresholds for utilities sector procurement
Concessions Directive defines threshold for concession contracts (EUR 5,538,000)
EU thresholds determine the boundary between full directive application and below-threshold regime
Public Contracts Directive parallels Utilities Directive — same legislative package, similar structure, different scope
Public Contracts Directive parallels Concessions Directive — same legislative package, lighter-touch regime for concessions
Public Contracts Directive defers to Defence Procurement Directive for defence and security contracts (lex specialis)
Remedies Directive (classic) provides review procedures for contracts under the Public Contracts Directive
Remedies Directive (utilities) provides review procedures for contracts under the Utilities Directive
Directive 2007/66/EC amends the classic sector Remedies Directive
Directive 2007/66/EC amends the utilities sector Remedies Directive
Directive 2007/66/EC introduced the mandatory standstill period into the Remedies Directives
Directive 2007/66/EC introduced contract ineffectiveness as a remedy
Directive 2007/66/EC introduced alternative penalties where ineffectiveness cannot be declared
Breach of standstill period may trigger contract ineffectiveness remedy
Standstill period enables aggrieved tenderers to seek interim measures before contract conclusion
Where ineffectiveness cannot be declared due to overriding general interest, alternative penalties are imposed instead
Interim measures (suspension) typically precede the set-aside decision on the merits
Voluntary ex ante transparency notice provides safe harbour against contract ineffectiveness
Mandatory exclusion may be overcome through self-cleaning measures under Art.57(6)
Discretionary exclusion may be overcome through self-cleaning measures under Art.57(6)
Selection criteria compliance is self-declared through the ESPD at tender stage
Non-application of exclusion grounds is self-declared through the ESPD at tender stage
MEAT award criteria may include life-cycle costing as a cost-effectiveness approach
MEAT framework enables environmental award criteria as part of green public procurement
MEAT framework enables social award criteria as part of socially responsible procurement
Technical specifications may include environmental characteristics supporting GPP
Technical specifications must be non-discriminatory and comply with equal treatment principle
Open procedure requires award based on MEAT criteria disclosed in contract notice/documents
Restricted procedure uses selection criteria to shortlist candidates for invitation to tender
Competitive procedure with negotiation builds upon the restricted procedure structure with added negotiation phase
Competitive dialogue is an alternative to competitive procedure with negotiation for complex procurements
Innovation partnership differs from negotiated procedures by combining R&D and commercial phases
Illegal use of negotiated procedure without publication (direct award) may trigger contract ineffectiveness
Breach of framework agreement call-off rules above specified values may trigger contract ineffectiveness
Dynamic purchasing systems must be operated as a completely electronic process
Electronic auctions are part of the broader e-procurement framework
eForms Regulation defines the standard notice formats published on TED
TED implements the transparency principle through centralised publication of procurement notices
E-procurement supports transparency through electronic access to documents and audit trails
Equal treatment principle requires transparency — all operators must have equal access to information
Equal treatment is threatened by conflicts of interest — hence Art.24 obligation to prevent and identify them
Contracting authorities are subject to the Public Contracts Directive
Economic operators submit the ESPD as self-declaration with their tenders/requests to participate
Abnormally low tenders must be rejected if low price results from non-compliance with social/labour law (Art.18(2))
Division into lots facilitates SME access to procurement opportunities
Contract modifications are constrained by transparency — substantial modifications must be published
In-house exception allows contracting authorities to award to controlled entities without procurement procedure
Anti-competitive agreements (bid-rigging) constitute a discretionary exclusion ground under Art.57(4)(d)
Competitive, transparent procurement generally excludes State aid — improper procurement may indicate illegal State aid
European Commission monitors and enforces correct transposition of the Public Contracts Directive by Member States
CJEU interprets the Public Contracts Directive through preliminary rulings
CJEU interprets the Remedies Directive through preliminary rulings
National review bodies derive their procurement review powers from the Remedies Directives
National review bodies grant interim measures in procurement disputes
National review bodies declare contract ineffectiveness in the most serious infringements
National review bodies award damages to persons harmed by procurement infringements
